articles.title: In Defense of Abolition
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: At the July DSA National Political Committee (NPC) meeting, I proposed adding abolition to the Workers Deserve More program because I believe that abolishing capitalist policing and prisons is a fundamental demand of the socialist movement. I crafted the language carefully to clarify that we mean abolishing policing and prisons as institutions of capitalist rule, not conflating the abolition of capitalist policing and prisons with the abolition of every future social capacity for accountability and safety. articles.title: Americans Are Turning Against School Vouchers
articles.author: Jennifer C. Berkshire
articles.content_excerpt: Ten percent. That’s how many Arizonans support that state’s Wild West voucher scheme. If the figure seems surprising given the ardency of the sales pitch for “education freedom,” its source should send your eyebrows skyward. This bleak view of Arizona public opinion about the state’s $1-billion-plus Education Savings Account (ESA) program comes not from voucher haters but from their superfans: the American Federation for Children (AFC), the deep-pocketed and highly influential school-choice lobbying firm started by Betsy DeVos. articles.title: Economics Needs a New Approach to Inflation
articles.author: Andrew Elrod
articles.content_excerpt: Four years have passed since the COVID-19 pandemic’s inflation in the wake of the American economy’s reopening hit its peak, and the American business cycle is today in a strange way. Wanting to slow the rise in prices that accompanied the reopening and construction boom, the Biden administration and the Federal Reserve cut social spending and raised interest rates. Nonresidential construction has been falling since late 2023. Residential construction investment collapsed in early 2023, then rose briefly in 2024, but has been falling for over a year now. articles.title: The Socialist Labor Unionists Who Took On Samuel Gompers
articles.author: Philipp Corfman
articles.content_excerpt: “We have started on a great big national fight with the union movement at stake!” Max Hayes, socialist newspaper editor and union leader, thundered to the assembled representatives of Cleveland, Ohio’s labor movement in the fall of 1909. “The American Federation of Labor will stand or fall as events issue.” The delegates roared their approval, setting in motion a decisive battle for the soul of organized labor. On one side were Cleveland’s radical left-wing workers, led by Hayes; on the other, the AFL, led by archconservative President Samuel Gompers.
